@{5af5f97d56feb85f40086953|full_name}: Depends on the count. I have a 60K poly model that lags a ton with no Dynamic Bones if any Shape Keys are used on it. This means if someone uses it to talk (Visemes) frames jump from 90 to 45 even if you're just alone in a world with a single directional real-time light. Meanwhile decimating it down to 40K for some magical reason lets everything work fine with both Blend Shapes and Dynamic Bones, literally just swapping the mesh out for one with 33% fewer polygons. I don't understand this at all, I assume it hit some kind of limit or wall that pushed it over the edge into being horrible.

That said, yeah, polygons without animators affecting them don't really matter.

I think the best solution to this is to integrate some of the common non-malicious features of popular VRLoader modules into the game. A lot of my friends use it only for the non-malicious features. An anti-cheat would be difficult to implement since VRC seems to be so easy to modify. Injectors will be hard to stop since they can inject code from DLL files that could be placed anywhere on your hard drive. I'm not too keen on VRC scanning the contents of my entire hard drive. 

Here is a list of features I've heard of from various friends about VRLoader that I think belong in the game:
-Flight (maybe if people get too butthurt about people flying around in maps they shouldn't, make it a per-world thing. We already got flying avatars so I don't see how much will change.)
-Unlimited favorites
-Personal avatar list optimizations (search, categorization, etc)
-Improved safety settings, shader blacklist, shader logger (to get names for blacklist)
-Teleport to player (but make it a request instead of forced)
-Cloning set to on or off for individual public avatars
